text:
maria: Heads-up — nightly evals started showing intermittent OOMs on worker-2 for the new quantized runs, ~10% of jobs. Not a consistent seed pattern.

eval-bot: nightly-eval | run 2026-03-19T03:12Z finished with 87% success. Failed jobs: 12. Logs: https://artifacts/redwood/nightly/1905432100/

ajay: I pulled a few logs, they all show CUDA OOM on allocation of kv cache after first batch. stack trace points to allocator.cu: allocate_kv.

linh: Can you paste a small log excerpt?

ajay: ```
ERROR: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 128MiB on device 0
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/harness/worker.py", line 312, in process_batch
    kv = allocator.alloc_kv(batch_size, seq_len)
  File "/app/harness/allocator.cu", line 89, in alloc_kv
    throw std::bad_alloc();
```

maria: Interesting thing: OOM only occurs when harness --workers > 1 and --reuse-contexts=true. If we force --workers=1 or --reuse-contexts=false the run passes. So maybe CUDA contexts are not released between tasks.

sarah: That smells like stale contexts or double-assignment of GPUs. Could the scheduler be assigning the same GPU to two workers simultaneously?

devon: Scheduler logs look ok — it assigns exclusive device ids per process. But there was a recent patch to the context pool that tries to keep contexts alive per-thread to reduce warmup. Maybe the pool returns shared context to different processes incorrectly when using fork + multiprocessing.

linh: Repro script: `python -m harness.run --model redwood-1q --workers 4 --reuse-contexts=true --seed 7` -> 1/10 runs OOMs. If I run under `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` it still happens, so double allocation on same device within process is possible.

ajay: Could be that context pool uses threading.local but our workers are spawned with 'forkserver' — threading.local isn't isolated across fork? Or vice versa. Need to verify worker creation method.

maria: Quick mitigation: add an env guard to disable context reuse in nightly until we fix. I pushed a tiny change to the nightly config: `REUSE_CONTEXTS=false` in CI.

devon: For triage, let's add extra debug to allocator: log current active contexts and their pids right before alloc_kv. That should tell us if contexts from other workers are present. Patch incoming.

linh: Also can reproduce locally with a loop launching 4 subprocesses that call a small C++ JNI wrapper alloc/free — if contexts leak between subprocesses that's a runtime bug. I'll spin that up now.

ajay: If we confirm it's a fork + context pooling issue, workaround is to switch to spawn-based worker start or ensure pool is reinitialized post-fork.

maria: Thanks. Devon/linh/ajay, coordinate on a minimal repro and we can roll a hotfix. Leaving the config change so nightly won't spam alerts. :thumbsup:
